name: Gatte Ki Sabzi
instructions: 1. Mix besan, turmeric, chili powder, ajwain, curd, oil, and salt to form a firm dough; roll into cylindrical logs.
2. Boil the logs in water for 10-12 minutes until they float, then remove and slice into small pieces (gatte).
3. Prepare a tadka by heating oil in a pan, adding cumin, mustard seeds, and hing.
4. Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté, then stir in the whisked yogurt with spices, stirring continuously to prevent curdling.
5. Add the sliced gattes to the gravy and simmer for 5-7 minutes.
6. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot with roti or steamed rice.
description: A staple dish from the arid regions of Rajasthan, Gatte Ki Sabzi was traditionally created as a substitute for fresh vegetables. The protein-rich besan dumplings symbolize the resourcefulness of Rajasthani cuisine, offering a flavorful and comforting meal often served during festivals and family gatherings.
